position: Office of Housing / Federal Housing Administration
proposal: The Mandate says Congress should ideally consider a fundamental statutory revision restricting FHA single-family mortgage insurance to first-time homebuyers, with HUD support, including moving the HECM program back into its own special risk insurance fund, revising loan limit determinations and providing statutory flexibility for shorter-term products that amortize faster, and abandoning the affirmative obligation authorities built into single-family programs across federal agencies and the government-sponsored enterprises (p. 510).

HECM moved to its own special risk insurance fund (p. 510; none found)
Revised single-family loan limit determinations (p. 510; none found)
Statutory flexibility for shorter-term amortizing products (p. 510; also listed in c15-12)
Abandonment of affirmative obligation authorities in single-family programs and GSEs (p. 510; AFFH is tracked in c15-01)

status_summary: No enacted law or bill restricting FHA single-family insurance to first-time homebuyers, moving HECM to its own fund, revising single-family loan limit determinations or adding shorter-term product flexibility was found. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, Public Law 119-101, became law without signature on 2026-07-11 after presentment on 2026-06-29; per the Congressional Research Service it touches FHA through Mutual Mortgage Insurance Fund capital reporting, counseling, appraisals, a small-dollar mortgage pilot and multifamily loan limits, and does not address the listed single-family items.

That clause is tracked in c15-01. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19.
